audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Urgot all seven stages in a lane Malphite wins 52.77% over 542 games, and it flatly contradicts the entry's own prose: mid says 'level 6 is the whole matchup' and late opens 'First item onward is mine.'
audit.why: Levels 1-3 are Urgot's and the entry explains why well. But a chart that never hands Malphite a single stage cannot sit above text claiming the last four stages outright, in a lane he wins.
audit.corrected: Urgot owns Levels 1 through 5. Level 6, first item and two items are Malphite's — which is what the prose already says and what 52.77% supports.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and mid put the Malphite stabilisation at 4-5 on 'the E attack-speed slow finally bites into his auto-driven shred', with no cooldowns anywhere in the entry for either side.
audit.why: The numbers change how you play the stage. Purge is 12s at rank 1 and falls to zero cooldown at rank 5 — there is no waiting it out later, only avoiding its 490 range. Disdain is his longest cooldown at 16s at rank 1 and it is his only reposition, so it, not Purge, is the cooldown you bait and count. Corrosive Charge is 10s at rank 1 from 800 range. Fear Beyond Death is 100/85/70s against your 130/115/100s, so his ultimate is back before yours at every rank.
audit.corrected: Disdain 16s at rank 1 is the cooldown to bait — his only reposition. Purge is 12s at rank 1 and zero at rank 5, so late you avoid its 490 range rather than wait it out. Corrosive Charge 10s from 800. Fear Beyond Death 100/85/70s to your 130/115/100s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet-flagged: the entry names none of Urgot's abilities, and the generic labels it uses are wrong about which button does what. 'His Q shotgun-leg pools and W passive shred' assigns the leg blasts to Q and calls W a passive.
audit.why: The leg blasts are Echoing Flames, his passive — 'Urgot's basic attacks and Purge periodically trigger blasts of flame from his legs'. Q is Corrosive Charge, an explosive charge fired at a location that damages and slows. W is Purge, an active, and the most exploitable thing in his kit is written right into it: 'Urgot slows himself while he unloads his weapon on nearby enemies'. A player told W is a passive will never realise that the moment Urgot commits to Purge he has slowed himself, and that 490 is a range he can be walked out of.
audit.corrected: Echoing Flames (P) is the leg blasts, off autos and Purge. Corrosive Charge (Q) is the ranged explosive with a slow, 800 range. Purge (W) is an active that slows Urgot himself while it fires, 490 range. Disdain (E) charges, shields him, and hurls you. Fear Beyond Death (R) impales and executes.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2], wants.you[1], mid and whys[4] all build the Level 6 spike on Urgot being 'immobile', 'dashless', someone who 'literally cannot sidestep the knock-up'.
audit.why: Disdain is movement: 'Urgot charges in a direction, shielding himself and trampling non-champion enemies.' He is not dashless — he has a 475-range charge on 16s that also shields him. The advice built on the false premise is close to right but for the wrong reason, and it teaches the player to ult on sight. The true version is sharper: he has exactly one reposition on a 16s cooldown, so R is guaranteed once Disdain is spent and merely likely before that.
audit.corrected: Urgot is not dashless — Disdain charges him 475 and shields him, on 16s at rank 1. Unstoppable Force is guaranteed once that is spent, which makes Disdain the cooldown you count before every R.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fear Beyond Death appears only as 'R-fear and execute' with no range and no threshold behaviour, in the one matchup where the enemy ultimate specifically hunts a low-health frontline.
audit.why: It is 2500 range and it impales the first champion hit, then becomes an execute only if that champion falls below a health threshold. That is a rule Malphite can actually play around: the danger is not the cast, it is being under the threshold when it lands, and 2500 range means there is no distance at which a low Malphite is safe. The entry's own late paragraph identifies the execute as the losing condition and then never tells the player what governs it.
audit.corrected: Fear Beyond Death impales from 2500 range and only executes if you are already under its health threshold — so the counterplay is your health bar, not your positioning.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 belong to Urgot and I just accept it. His Q shotgun-leg pools and W passive shred deal percent-max-HP, which carves through my Granite Shield faster than any flat-damage laner, so I do not try to trade — I last-hit at max range and let the shield refresh whenever he backs off. Never walk into his E flip range while my W and E are still locked; eating a flip pre-6 means a full sustained-DPS combo I have no answer to. Farm, hold the shield, and wait for my buttons.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 belong to Urgot and you accept it. Corrosive Charge (Q) pokes from 800 to your 625, and Echoing Flames — his passive, not his Q — adds leg blasts to every auto and to Purge. Purge (W) is an active on 12s at rank 1, and the tell is in its own text: it slows Urgot while it fires, so a committed Purge is a slowed Urgot at 490 range. Do not walk into Disdain (E) while Thunderclap and Ground Slam are still locked; a flip pre-6 is a full combo you cannot answer. Farm, hold the shield, wait for your buttons.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 I stabilize — W Thunderclap gives me bonus armor and AoE on-hits, and E Ground Slam's attack-speed slow finally bites into his auto-driven shred, so I can farm through his poke instead of bleeding to it. It is still reactive, not dominant; respect the E flip. Then level 6 is the whole matchup: Unstoppable Force lands clean on an immobile, dashless Urgot who literally cannot sidestep the knock-up, and that is the kill pressure I never had pre-6. Bait his E flip, then R him into my tower and chunk him while he is locked.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 you stabilise: Thunderclap gives armour and aftershocks on your next autos, and Ground Slam is a flat 7s whose attack-speed cut finally bites into Echoing Flames. It is parity, not dominance — respect Disdain, 16s at rank 1 and 475 range. Level 6 is the matchup. Urgot is not dashless, but Disdain is his only reposition, so count it: once he has spent it, Unstoppable Force is guaranteed. Bait the charge, then R him toward your tower and chunk him while he is locked down.

edits.before: First item onward is mine. An armor item plus my W armor-scaling on-hits and E slow turn me into a frontline that out-trades his shotgun legs, and the more armor I stack the less his auto-shred matters. The one honest caveat: Urgot's Q/W are percent-max-HP and his R fears and executes, so in a long, drawn-out DPS slugfest a fed Urgot can still grind my low-economy body down once my cooldowns are spent. So I do not stand and trade forever — I use R to engage on my terms or to flank his carries in teamfights, where my knock-up and E slow swing the fight rather than feeding his sustained damage.
edits.after: First item onward is yours. An armour item plus Thunderclap’s armour-scaling on-hits makes you a frontline that out-trades Echoing Flames, and Ground Slam grows off exactly the same stat, so one purchase does both jobs. Two caveats keep you honest. Purge has no cooldown at all by rank 5, so late there is nothing to wait out — you simply stay outside its 490 range. And Fear Beyond Death impales from 2500 and only executes if you are already under its health threshold, which means the counterplay is your health bar rather than your spacing. Use R to open fights or to flank his carries, never to start a slugfest.

notes: Packet defect confirmed: none of Urgot's abilities were named, and the generic labels the entry used assigned the wrong effects to the wrong buttons. The leg blasts are Echoing Flames, his passive — the entry called them 'Q shotgun-leg pools'. Purge was called a 'W passive' throughout; it is an active on 12s at rank 1 whose own text hands you the counterplay ('Urgot slows himself while he unloads his weapon on nearby enemies') and which reaches zero cooldown at rank 5, so late it is a range to leave rather than a cooldown to wait out. SECOND CORRECTION: four strings build the Level 6 spike on Urgot being 'immobile', 'dashless', unable to 'sidestep' the knock-up. Disdain charges him 475 units and shields him. The conclusion survives but the reason changes, and the corrected version is more useful: he has exactly one reposition on 16s, so count Disdain and your R is guaranteed after it. THIRD: Fear Beyond Death was only ever 'R-fear and execute'. It impales from 2500 and executes only below a health threshold, which means the counterplay is your health bar rather than your spacing. UNVERIFIED, DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE: seven strings describe Corrosive Charge and Purge as dealing percent-max-HP damage. Riot's text says only 'physical damage' for both and urgot.json carries no percentHealth flag — but an absent derived flag means unknown, not absent, so I neither repeated the claim in my rewrites nor contradicted it. The full layer's tldr ('His W shreds your HP') rests on the same unverified claim. This needs a ruling before anyone writes itemisation advice from it. VOICE: early, mid and late were in the first person ('I', 'my'); my rewrites are in the site's second person. NOT EDITED: the chart gives Urgot all seven stages while the prose says 'level 6 is the whole matchup' and 'First item onward is mine' — win[4] through win[6] should read Malphite. Enum values, outside the length band.
